questions.stem: What kind of image is formed by a convex mirror regardless of the object's position?
questions.solution: A convex mirror always forms a virtual and erect image, no matter where the object is placed. This is because the reflecting surface of a convex mirror curves outward, causing the light rays to diverge after reflection. A real image requires the light rays to converge, which does not happen in a convex mirror. An inverted image would require the light rays to converge in a specific way, which is also not the case here. A virtual image is formed when the light rays appear to come from a point behind the mirror, which is what happens in a convex mirror.

hi.solution: एक उत्तल दर्पण हमेशा एक आभासी और सीधी छवि बनाता है, चाहे वस्तु कहाँ रखी जाए। यह इसलिए है क्योंकि एक उत्तल दर्पण की परावर्तक सतह बाहर की ओर वक्र होती है, जिसके कारण परावर्तन के बाद प्रकाश की किरणें बिखर जाती हैं। एक वास्तविक छवि के लिए प्रकाश की किरणों के अभिसरण की आवश्यकता होती है, जो उत्तल दर्पण में नहीं होता है। उल्टी छवि के लिए प्रकाश की किरणों के एक विशिष्ट तरीके से अभिसरण की आवश्यकता होती है, जो यहाँ भी नहीं होता है। आभासी छवि तब बनती है जब प्रकाश की किरणें दर्पण के पीछे के एक बिंदु से आती हुई लगती हैं, जो उत्तल दर्पण में होता है।

questions.stem: A student places an object 3 cm in front of a concave mirror. What kind of image is likely to be formed?
questions.solution: When an object is placed very close to a concave mirror (within the focal length), the image formed is virtual and erect. This happens because the light rays diverge after reflection and appear to come from a point behind the mirror. A real image would require the light rays to converge, which does not happen in this case. An inverted image is formed when the object is placed beyond the focal length, which is not the case here. A real and erect image is not possible with a concave mirror.

questions.stem: If a person holds a concave mirror facing the Sun and directs the reflected light onto a piece of paper, what is the effect on the paper?
questions.solution: A concave mirror converges parallel rays of sunlight to a single point, concentrating the energy. This concentration of light can generate enough heat to cause the paper to start burning. The other options are incorrect because they do not align with the physical properties of light and heat transfer.

questions.stem: Based on the description of spherical mirrors, which of the following is true about concave mirrors?
choices: They can form both real and virtual images
They can only form inverted images
questions.solution: Concave mirrors can form both real and virtual images depending on the position of the object. When the object is placed within the focal length, the image is virtual and erect. When the object is placed beyond the focal length, the image is real and inverted. This is different from convex mirrors, which always form virtual and erect images. Concave mirrors do not always form real images, nor do they always form virtual images. They are also not limited to forming only inverted images.

questions.stem: A concave lens always produces an image that is erect and diminished in size. What happens to the size of the image as the object moves farther away from the lens?
questions.solution: A concave lens always produces an erect and diminished image, regardless of the object's position. As the object moves farther away from the lens, the image becomes smaller. questions.stem: A concave mirror forms a real, inverted, and diminished image. Where is the object likely placed?
choices: Between the focal point and the mirror
Between the centre of curvature and the focal point
questions.solution: When an object is placed beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror, the image formed is real, inverted, and diminished. This is because the light rays converge at a point between the focal point and the centre of curvature. When the object is at the focal point, the image is formed at infinity. When the object is between the focal point and the mirror, the image is virtual and erect. When the object is between the centre of curvature and the focal point, the image is real, inverted, and enlarged.
